findings.title: Exclusivity clause risks employee misclassification
findings.deviation: Clause 3.1 requires the contractor to work exclusively for AtliQ, preventing any other professional engagements during the term.
findings.impact: This extreme restriction risks legally reclassifying the freelancer as an employee under US labor laws.
findings.quote: During the term of this Agreement, the Contractor shall devote his professional working time exclusively to the Company and shall not, directly or indirectly, provide services to, or be engaged or employed by, any other person, firm or company, whether paid or unpaid, without the Company's prior written consent.
findings.counterPosition: Delete Clause 3.1 entirely to ensure the contractor remains an independent contractor.

findings.title: Worldwide post-termination non-compete is overly restrictive
findings.deviation: Clause 8.1 imposes a 12-month post-termination worldwide non-compete on the contractor.
findings.impact: Such a broad restrictive covenant is highly disfavored under US labor standards and increases the risk of employee misclassification.
findings.quote: For a period of twelve (12) months after termination or expiry of this Agreement, the Contractor shall not, anywhere in the world, directly or indirectly, provide any software or data services to any person, whether as an employee, consultant, contractor, partner or otherwise, in competition with the Company.
findings.counterPosition: Delete the post-termination non-compete obligation in Clause 8.1.

findings.title: Highly unequal and one-sided termination notice periods
findings.deviation: Clause 9.1 allows AtliQ to terminate on 24 hours' notice, while Clause 9.2 requires the contractor to give 60 days' notice.
findings.impact: This extreme imbalance is highly unfair and strongly indicates an employment relationship rather than an independent contractor arrangement.
findings.quote: 9.1 The Company may terminate this Agreement at any time by giving twenty-four (24) hours' written notice (including by email) to the Contractor. 9.2 The Contractor may terminate this Agreement by giving sixty (60) days' written notice to the Company.
findings.counterPosition: Amend both notice periods to be mutual, such as 30 days' written notice for convenience by either party.

findings.title: Missing flow-down of client's data security and incident requirements
findings.deviation: The agreement fails to flow down specific compliance with the Illinois Personal Information Protection Act, Lakeshore's security standard, and the 72-hour security incident notification timeline.
findings.impact: AtliQ could face severe liability if the contractor fails to secure client data or report a security incident within the client's strict timelines.
findings.quote: 5.1 The Contractor shall perform the Services diligently and to a professional standard, and comply with the Company's reasonable instructions, security policies and the policies of the Company's clients notified to him. 5.2 The Contractor shall use his own equipment unless otherwise agreed, and shall access client systems only through Company-approved environments.
findings.counterPosition: Add an explicit data protection schedule requiring the contractor to comply with the Illinois Personal Information Protection Act, Lakeshore's security requirements, and to report any security incident to AtliQ within 24 hours.
findings.linkedQuote: 12.1 Vendor shall comply with Lakeshore's Information Security Requirements (Exhibit C) and applicable privacy laws, including the Illinois Personal Information Protection Act. 12.2 Vendor shall notify Lakeshore within seventy-two (72) hours of discovering any unauthorized access to Lakeshore Data.

findings.title: Missing flow-down license for contractor pre-existing tools
findings.deviation: The agreement does not grant AtliQ a license to use or pass along the contractor's pre-existing tools or libraries incorporated into deliverables.
findings.impact: AtliQ cannot legally grant the perpetual, non-exclusive license to Lakeshore for pre-existing tools used by the contractor.
findings.quote: 6.1 All work product, code, pipelines, documentation, reports and other materials created by the Contractor in the course of the Services ("Work Product") shall vest in the Company upon creation. 6.2 The Contractor hereby assigns to the Company all present and future right, title and interest in the Work Product, including all intellectual property rights, worldwide and for the full term of such rights, and waives any moral rights therein. The assignment shall not lapse under Section 19(4) of the Copyright Act, 1957 if the rights are not exercised within one year.
findings.counterPosition: Add a license clause for pre-existing materials, granting AtliQ a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable license to use and sublicense any contractor pre-existing tools.
findings.linkedQuote: 7.2 Vendor retains all rights in its pre-existing tools, code libraries and methodologies ("Vendor Tools"). Vendor grants Lakeshore a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use any Vendor Tools incorporated in the Deliverables for Lakeshore's internal business purposes.

findings.title: Contractor agreement precedes execution of the main client contract
findings.deviation: The contractor agreement is being finalized and dated prior to the signing or execution of the underlying Lakeshore MSA.
findings.impact: AtliQ risks being financially bound to pay the contractor without having an active, revenue-generating client contract in place.
findings.quote: This Independent Contractor Agreement ("Agreement") is made on ____________, 2026 (the "Effective Date") between:
findings.counterPosition: Add a condition precedent stating that the agreement is contingent upon and shall only become effective once the Lakeshore Grocers Inc. MSA is fully executed.
findings.linkedQuote: This Master Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is made as of ____________, 2026 (the "Effective Date") between:

fine.note: No delay liquidated damages are included, which aligns with AtliQ's preference.
The contractor indemnifies AtliQ for their own errors and intellectual property, without requiring AtliQ to indemnify for its own negligence.
Confidentiality obligations are standard and protect AtliQ's and its clients' data.
Contractor warrants standard professional performance and compliance of the services.
No unilateral set-off rights are given to the contractor.
Subcontracting is strictly prohibited without prior written consent, meeting client expectations.
